action: A court case that is not an application. The civil rules say it includes cases started by a statement of claim, notice of action, counterclaim, crossclaim, or third or later party claim. The Courts of Justice Act list also includes a claim and a divorce petition or counterpetition.
address: In the family rules, a person's address covers their street or municipal address, mailing address, telephone number, fax number and email address.
adverse effect: In the Limitations Act, this term has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection Act.
appellant: The person who brings, or starts, an appeal. The civil rules and the family rules both use the word this way.
appellate court: In the civil rules, this means the Court of Appeal or the Divisional Court, depending on the circumstances.
applicant: The person who makes, or starts, an application. The civil rules and the family rules both use the word this way.
application: In the civil rules, a case started by a notice of application; the Courts of Justice Act says a civil case started by notice of application or by application. In the family rules, it can mean the document that starts a case, or the process for bringing a new case to court for a final or provisional order.
arbitration agreement: In the family rules, an agreement where two or more people agree to send a dispute between them to arbitration. The dispute can be one that has already come up or one that may come up later.
assault: In the Limitations Act, the word assault includes a battery.
bond: In the family rules, a bond includes a recognizance. Wording about posting a bond also covers entering into a recognizance.
case: In the family rules, a case is an application or any other legally allowed way of bringing a matter to court for a final or provisional order. It includes all the motions, enforcements and appeals that are part of it.
certificate of appointment of estate tru: In the civil rules, this covers letters probate, letters of administration, and letters of administration with the will annexed. It also includes a small estate certificate or an amended small estate certificate.
child: In the family rules, a child is defined by the law governing the case, or else a person under 18; Divorce Act cases include a "child of the marriage". The Family Law Act adds someone a parent has shown a settled intention to treat as their family's child, except a child placed in paid foster care by a lawful custodian.
child protection case: In the family rules, a case under Part V of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
child support guidelines: In the family rules, either Ontario's Child Support Guidelines regulation under the Family Law Act or the Federal Child Support Guidelines, depending on the case. The Family Law Act describes them as the guidelines set by regulations made under that Act.
claim: In the Limitations Act, a claim is a claim to remedy an injury, loss or damage that happened because of something someone did or failed to do.
clerk: In the family rules, a clerk is anyone who has the authority of a clerk or a registrar of the court.
cohabit: In the Family Law Act, to cohabit means to live together in a conjugal relationship, whether the two people are married or not.
contaminant: In the Limitations Act, this term has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection Act.
contempt motion: In the family rules, a motion asking the court for a contempt order.
contempt order: In the family rules, an order finding that a person is in contempt of court.
continuing record: In the family rules, the record set up under those rules that holds the written documents in a case that are filed with the court.
county: In the civil rules, county includes a district, a regional or district municipality, and the City of Toronto.
court: Small Claims rules: the Small Claims Court; civil rules: the court where the case is pending, including an associate judge in the Superior Court of Justice; family rules: the court hearing the case. The Family Law Act names the Ontario Court of Justice, the Family Court of the Superior Court of Justice or the Superior Court of Justice, though some parts of it (Parts I and II) do not include the Ontario Court of Justice.
default hearing: In the family rules, a hearing under the Family Responsibility and Support Arrears Enforcement Act, 1996 where a payor is required to come to court and explain why they have not paid as a support order requires.
defendant: The person an action is started against. The civil rules and the Courts of Justice Act both use the word this way.
deliver: In the civil rules, to deliver a document means to serve it and file it with proof of service. Delivery has the matching meaning.
dependant: In the Family Law Act's support part, a dependant is a person whom another person has an obligation to support under that part.
Director of the Family Responsibility Of: In the family rules, the Director of the Family Responsibility Office under the Family Responsibility and Support Arrears Enforcement Act, 1996. The word Director on its own means the same, unless the context shows otherwise.
disability: In the Small Claims rules and the civil rules, a person under a disability is a minor; someone mentally incapable, as defined in the Substitute Decisions Act, 1992, about an issue in the case, whether or not they have a guardian; or an absentee under the Absentees Act.
discharge: In the Limitations Act, this term has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection Act.
discovery: In the civil rules, discovery covers discovery of documents, examination for discovery, inspection of property, and medical examination of a party, as the rules provide.
document: In the Small Claims rules and the civil rules, a document includes data and information in electronic form. In the family rules, it means information, sound or images recorded by any method.
domestic contract: In the family rules and the Family Law Act, this means a domestic contract as defined in the Domestic Contracts part (Part IV) of the Family Law Act.
electronic: In the Small Claims rules and the civil rules, electronic includes things created, recorded, sent or stored in digital or other non-physical form by electronic, magnetic or optical means, or by any means with similar abilities. Electronically has the matching meaning.
enforcement: In the family rules, enforcement means using one or more of the remedies listed in the enforcement rule to enforce an order.
environmental claim: In the Limitations Act, a claim based on something done or not done that caused, contributed to, or allowed the discharge of a contaminant into the natural environment, where that has caused or is likely to cause an adverse effect.
factum: In the civil rules, a factum includes a book of authorities, when the rules require one.
family arbitration: In the family rules, an arbitration about matters that could be covered in a marriage contract, separation agreement, cohabitation agreement or paternity agreement under the Family Law Act, and that is carried out only under the law of Ontario or another Canadian jurisdiction.
family legal services provider: In the family rules, a paralegal authorized under the Law Society Act to provide specific family legal services.
file: In the family rules, to file means to file a document, with proof of service where service is required, either at the court office in the municipality where the case or enforcement started or was transferred to, or electronically as the rules allow.
final order: In the family rules, an order, other than a temporary order, that decides a claim in an application. It includes an order made on a motion that changes a final order, a judgment, and an order deciding a party's rights in an issue between parties or between a party and a non-party.
government agency: In the family rules, this means the Crown, a Crown agency, a municipal government or agency, a children's aid society, or any other public body.
hearing: In the civil rules, a hearing means the hearing of an application, motion, reference, appeal or assessment of costs, or a trial. The Courts of Justice Act says a hearing includes a trial.
holiday: In the Small Claims rules and the civil rules, holidays include every Saturday and Sunday, named days such as New Year's Day, Good Friday, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day, and specially proclaimed holidays. When certain holidays fall on a weekend, or Christmas falls on a Friday, the following Monday (sometimes also Tuesday) is a holiday.
income source: In the family rules, this term has the same meaning as in the Family Responsibility and Support Arrears Enforcement Act, 1996.
international child abduction case: In the family rules, an application about a child allegedly wrongfully taken to, or kept in, Ontario, made under the Children's Law Reform Act or the Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, when the taking or keeping involves a place outside Canada.
judge: In the civil rules, a judge of the court. It does not include an associate judge.
judgment: In the civil rules, a decision that finally ends an application or action on its merits. It includes a judgment entered because a party was in default.
lawyer: A person authorized under the Law Society Act to practise law in Ontario. The civil rules and the family rules both use the word this way.
lawyer's office: In the civil rules, the office of the lawyer of record, as shown in the last document that lawyer filed.
legal aid rate: In the family rules, the rate Legal Aid Ontario pays on a service provider's account for copying done in the service provider's office.
licensed representative: In the family rules, a lawyer or a family legal services provider.
limited scope retainer: In the civil rules, a lawyer providing legal services for part, but not all, of a client's legal matter, by agreement between the lawyer and the client.
matrimonial home: In the Family Law Act, a matrimonial home as described in a specific section of that Act. It also includes property that was a matrimonial home under that section on the valuation date.
motion: A motion in a proceeding or an intended proceeding. The civil rules and the Courts of Justice Act both use the word this way.
moving party: In the civil rules, the person who makes a motion.
municipality: In the family rules, a county, district, district municipality, regional municipality, the City of Toronto, or a municipal corporation formed by merging all the municipalities of one of these. It also includes an Indian reserve within a municipality's area and the part of the Niagara region that was once the County of Lincoln.
net family property: In the Family Law Act, the value of property a spouse owns on the valuation date, except certain excluded property, minus their debts and liabilities, and minus the value of property (other than a matrimonial home) owned at marriage. That marriage-date value is reduced by debts then owed, except debts tied directly to buying or significantly improving a matrimonial home.
on motion: In the family rules, on motion means on a motion made by a party or by a person who has an interest in the case.
order: In the Small Claims rules and the civil rules, an order includes a judgment. The Courts of Justice Act says it includes a judgment or decree.
originating process: In the civil rules, a document that starts a proceeding, such as a statement of claim, notice of action, notice of application, an estate trustee or small estate certificate application, a counterclaim against a non-party, or a third or later party claim. It does not include a crossclaim, a notice of motion, or a counterclaim only against existing parties.
paralegal: A person licensed (Small Claims rules) or authorized (family rules) under the Law Society Act to provide legal services in Ontario.
parent: In the Family Law Act, a parent includes someone who has shown a settled intention to treat a child as a child of their family, except where the child was placed in a foster home for payment by a person with lawful custody.
payment order: In the family rules, a temporary or final order, but not a provisional one, requiring a person to pay money to another. It includes things like support orders, support deduction orders, contempt fines, forfeiture of a bond, orders to pay the fees and expenses of a court-named assessor, mediator or other expert or of a person doing a parentage blood test, and costs in a case.
payor: In the family rules, a person required to pay money under an order or agreement, including the estate trustee of a payor who has died.
periodic payment: In the family rules, an amount payable at regular intervals, including an amount payable in instalments.
person: In the civil rules, a person includes a party to a proceeding.
plaintiff: The person who starts an action. The civil rules and the Courts of Justice Act both use the word this way.
proceeding: In the civil rules, a proceeding means either an action or an application.
proof of service: In the Small Claims rules, proof that a document was served, given in the way a specific Small Claims rule sets out.
property: In the Family Law Act's family property part, any present or future interest in real or personal property, including property a spouse controls through certain powers, and the family-law value of a spouse's pension interest from the marriage date to the valuation date. In the matrimonial home part, it means real or personal property.
property claim: In the family rules, a claim under Part I of the Family Law Act, a claim for a constructive or resulting trust, or a claim for money as compensation for unjust enrichment.
provisional order: In the family rules, an order that does not take effect until a court confirms it.
recipient: In the family rules, a person entitled to receive money or costs under a payment order or agreement. It includes things like a person receiving support money for a child's benefit, certain agencies, a children's aid society, an assessor, mediator or other expert owed fees, and the estate trustee of someone who was owed money when they died.
referee: In the civil rules, the person to whom a reference in a proceeding is directed.
region: In the Courts of Justice Act, a region means a region officially set (prescribed) under that Act.
registrar: In the civil rules, the Registrar of the Divisional Court or the Court of Appeal, or a local registrar of the Superior Court of Justice, depending on the circumstances.
Registrar General: In the family rules, the Registrar General under the Vital Statistics Act.
regulations: In the Family Law Act, the regulations made under that Act.
representative: In the Small Claims rules, the lawyer, paralegal or other person representing someone in a Small Claims proceeding.
respondent: In the civil rules, the person an application is made against or an appeal is brought against. In the family rules, the person a claim is made against in an application, answer or appeal.
responding party: In the civil rules, the person a motion is made against.
special party: In the family rules, a party, other than a child party, who is or appears to be mentally incapable under the Substitute Decisions Act, 1992 about an issue in the case, and who needs legal representation as a result.
spouse: In the Family Law Act, either of two people who are married, or who entered a void or voidable marriage, if the person relying on this acted in good faith. The support part also covers two unmarried people who cohabited continuously for at least three years, or in a relationship of some permanence as parents of a child.
statute: In the civil rules, statute includes a law passed by the Parliament of Canada.
support deduction order: In the family rules, a support deduction order as defined in the Family Responsibility and Support Arrears Enforcement Act, 1996.
support order: In the family rules, a support order described in the Family Law Act, or a support order as defined in the Divorce Act (Canada) or the Family Responsibility and Support Arrears Enforcement Act, 1996.
temporary order: In the family rules, an order that says it is in effect only for a limited time. It includes an interim order.
territorial division: In the Small Claims rules, a county, district or regional municipality, plus certain listed areas as they existed on December 31, 2002, such as the City of Ottawa, the City of Toronto, the City of Hamilton and the Municipality of Chatham-Kent.
timetable: In the civil rules, a schedule for finishing one or more steps needed to move a proceeding forward, such as delivering affidavits of documents, examinations under oath (where available), or motions. It is set by a court order, or by a written agreement of the parties that does not go against an order.
trial: In the family rules, a trial includes a hearing.
trial sitting: In the family rules, the period of time the court sets during which a trial will be scheduled.
uncontested trial: In the family rules, a trial where only the party making the claim gives evidence and submissions.
valuation date: In the Family Law Act, the earliest of: the date spouses separate with no reasonable prospect of living together again; the date a divorce is granted; the date the marriage is declared a nullity; the date a spouse starts an improvident depletion application that is later granted; or the day before one spouse dies while the other survives.
will: In the civil rules, a will includes any testamentary document for which probate or administration may be granted.
